Rules I had to settle (both parsers identical, worth an architect look): (1) a value is parsed structured first and re-read as Expr only when the next token continues it (. .. { ( [ * ~ < > = ! | & + - / % : ?); a word, number or string after a value is a missing-comma error; (2) recovery skips to the next word in column 1 at or after the error; a missing '}' is reported where the next record starts, with a hint naming the open brace; (3) a one-line record's value must start on the '=' line (otherwise 'item.c =' took the next record as its expr); a top-level expr ends at the first line break outside brackets; (4) unit factors are exact reduced fractions, a number with a unit has at most 9 digits and 6 decimals (keeps int64), plain integers to int64; (5) an unknown word after a number is 'unknown unit' unless = { . follows (then missing comma); (6) a block key may be set once; a dotted lhs and a later block of the same name merge, a leaf set twice is an error; (7) columns count characters; errors sorted by position; a record with an error is dropped; (8) PeoRecord has one_line (canonical prints its value under '='), PeoValue is one struct with number/high/dimension/text/items/fields. open: none for this item; content conversion is PEO-136
